claim_verdicts.evidence: Overview: "time series collection happens via a pull model over HTTP". Configuration: "[ scrape_interval: <duration> | default = <global_config.scrape_interval> ]". Live lab (Prometheus 3.5.5, /api/v1/status/buildinfo): timestamp(http_requests_received_total) - timestamp(up{job="api"}) = 0 for every series, and timestamp(up) = lastScrape of the target (…48.328) -> samples stored with the scrape time.

git show stage-2:deploy/monitoring/prometheus.yml: lines 1-11 identical to the lesson block: global scrape_interval: 5s; scrape_configs: - job_name: api / static_configs: - targets: ["api:8080"]. Live /api/v1/status/config shows the same loaded config.

Configuration: "[ metrics_path: <path> | default = /metrics ]", "[ scheme: <scheme> | default = http ]". Live /api/v1/status/config (3.5.5) for job api: "metrics_path: /metrics", "scheme: http"; /api/v1/targets: "scrapeUrl":"http://api:8080/metrics".

"When Prometheus scrapes a target, it attaches some labels automatically to the scraped time series which serve to identify the scraped target: job: The configured job name that the target belongs to." Live query up returns {instance="api:8080", job="api"}.
"up{job="<job-name>", instance="<instance-id>"}: 1 if the instance is healthy, i.e. reachable, or 0 if the scrape failed." Captured output after docker compose stop api: "0" and "health=down".

Data model: "Every time series is uniquely identified by its metric name and optional key-value pairs called labels." "Each sample consists of: a float64 or native histogram value [and] a millisecond-precision timestamp". "The change of any label's value, including adding or removing labels, will create a new time series."

"Remember that every unique combination of key-value label pairs represents a new time series, which can dramatically increase the amount of data stored. Do not use labels to store dimensions with high cardinality (many different label values), such as user IDs, email addresses, or other unbounded sets of values."

refs profiles.md: "Services without a `profiles` attribute are always enabled."; "$ docker compose --profile debug up". stage-2 docker-compose.yml: profiles: [monitoring] on prometheus (246), grafana (263), loki (285), alloy (298); scripts/up.sh:16 `docker compose up -d --build --wait` names no profile. Lesson now says "leaves them out of a plain docker compose up", "starts them too" - no exclusivity.

git show stage-2:docker-compose.yml:242-253: image prom/prometheus:v3.5.5, profiles: [monitoring], volumes ./deploy/monitoring/prometheus.yml:/etc/prometheus/prometheus.yml:ro, ports "9090:9090", networks donhang ipv4_address 172.28.0.21. Target is api:8080, not caddy.

HTTP API: /api/v1/query value "[ <unix_time>, \"<sample_value>\" ]"; /api/v1/targets lists activeTargets. Live read-only curl (3.5.5): labels.job "api", scrapeUrl "http://api:8080/metrics", health "up", scrapeInterval "5s". Script @stage-2 l.10 jq() { docker compose exec -T lab jq "$@"; } shadows jq for l.12/23/36; lab has no profiles (always on). docker compose exec -T lab: /usr/bin/jq, jq-1.8.1, owned by jq-1.8.1-r0 (base image, not lab/Dockerfile apk list). Round 3: q1 "values" matches §4 "adds one value".

Captured output matches the lesson's text block line for line (job=api url=http://api:8080/metrics interval=5s health=up / 1 / 0 / health=down). Script line 33: trap 'docker compose start api 2>/dev/null && wait_for_up 1' EXIT. Not re-run (lab shared; caller forbade running the script).

Overview: "time series collection happens via a pull model over HTTP". Live /api/v1/status/config: the only scrape_config is job api with static_configs targets api:8080, metrics_path /metrics; no log source configured in Prometheus (logs go to Loki via Alloy).

Captured output shows up 0 and health=down after the stop; live config: scrape_interval 5s, scrape_timeout 5s, so a failed scrape is recorded within ~5-10 s. Script not re-run (shared lab, forbidden by caller); relied on the capture.
